prompt: What separates an agent from an assistant, in the sense this lesson uses?
hint: Ask who decides what happens next.

choices.text: An agent runs on a larger and more capable model than an assistant does
choices.why: Both can use the same model. The assistant and the agent in this lesson both call llama3.2:3b.

choices.text: The model chooses the next step, inside a loop
choices.why: Right. The defining move is that the model decides what happens next, and keeps deciding until it answers.

choices.text: Nobody has to read what it produces
choices.why: That is not part of the definition, and an agent's mistakes cost more, because it acts on them.

choices.text: It talks to customers directly
choices.why: Who reads the output is a deployment choice. An assistant talking to a customer still chooses no steps.

prompt: A nightly job reads yesterday's orders, and for every order delivered more than 30 days ago it closes the return window. It calls a model to word the email it sends. Which of the three is it?

choices.text: An agent, because a model takes part in what reaches the customer
choices.why: A model in the pipeline does not make it an agent. The model never chooses which step comes next.

choices.text: An assistant, because the model's part is to write text
choices.why: An assistant's draft goes to a person who decides. Here nobody reads the email before it is sent.

choices.text: Automation with a model call inside
choices.why: Right. The programmer wrote the order of the steps; the model fills in one of them.

choices.text: None of them: it starts by itself
choices.why: How it starts does not matter. What matters is who decides the steps, and here the code does.

prompt: A colleague asks whether a product is an agent. Which check settles it?

choices.text: Whether its documentation calls it one
choices.why: Names are marketing. This lesson's agent.py is forty lines and calls itself nothing.

choices.text: Whether it has more than one tool
choices.why: A loop with a single tool is an agent when the model decides when to call it and when to stop.

choices.text: Whether the line that picks the next step reads the model's reply
choices.why: Right. If the next step depends on what the model returned, the model is steering.

choices.text: Whether it streams its answer
choices.why: Streaming is how text arrives, and says nothing about who decides the steps.

prompt: `automation.py` was given `"the book I bought last week"` and stopped with `LookupError: no order the book I bought last week`. What does that show?

choices.text: The database is missing the order the customer placed last week
choices.why: The database was never asked about last week. The program passed the whole sentence as an order id.

choices.text: shop.py is broken and raises an error on valid input
choices.why: The input is not a valid order id. get_order raised exactly what it says.

choices.text: It handles only inputs its author foresaw
choices.why: Right. The path expects an order id; a sentence is outside the path, and nothing in it chooses another one.

choices.text: It should have retried
choices.why: Retrying the same lookup with the same string gives the same error.

prompt: The assistant's draft tells Bia she has until 24 October. Which part of that answer did nothing in the program check?

choices.text: The thirty days, which the model may have remembered wrongly
choices.why: The thirty days are in the help centre the assistant was given, word for word.

choices.text: The steps for sending the parcel back, which no tool returned
choices.why: They are in the same article: the prepaid label and the post office.

choices.text: That returns are free
choices.why: The article says so. The draft repeated it rather than inventing it.

choices.text: The delivery date, which came from Bia's message and was never compared with the order
choices.why: Right. The assistant had the help centre and the message, not the order. The person who sends the draft is the check.

prompt: Asked which ways she can pay, the agent searched the help centre. Asked about M-1043, it looked the order up. What made the first steps different?
hint: Look at what each message named.

choices.text: search_help ranked the payment article first for both questions
choices.why: search_help only ranks articles against the query it is given. It was not called for M-1043.

choices.text: The model read the message and chose a tool to match it
choices.why: Right. One message named an order and the other did not. The same agent.py took two paths.

choices.text: Two programs, one written for each kind of question
choices.why: Both runs were the same agent.py. Nothing in it mentions orders or payments.

choices.text: The order lookup failed, so the agent fell back on the search
choices.why: Nothing failed. Each run's first step succeeded and was followed by an answer.

prompt: In the vocabulary this lesson borrows from Anthropic's article, what is a workflow?

choices.text: Any program that calls a model more than once to finish a task
choices.why: Calling a model twice says nothing about who decides the order. An agent also calls it many times.

choices.text: An agent that was handed a written plan of the steps to follow
choices.why: A plan the model follows is still the model's choice of steps; a workflow's order is fixed in code.

choices.text: The visual editor some vendors sell for building agents by dragging boxes
choices.why: Some products use the word for that, but the distinction here is about who decides the path.

choices.text: Steps joined by paths written in code
choices.why: Right. The steps include model calls; the order of the steps is the programmer's.

prompt: A support tool asks the model to classify each message as `return`, `delivery` or `payment`, then runs a fixed procedure for each class. Where on the dial is it?

choices.text: A workflow with routing: one model choice among branches the programmer wrote
choices.why: Right. The model chooses the branch once; the programmer wrote every branch and their order.

choices.text: Fully an agent, since the model's output decides what runs
choices.why: The model picks a branch once, and never sees a result or chooses again. That is far short of a loop.

choices.text: Fully automation, since the procedures are code
choices.why: The branch taken depends on the model's reading, so the model holds one decision.

choices.text: An assistant, as a label is text
choices.why: Nobody reads the label in this design. The procedure runs on it directly.

prompt: Why does the lesson describe autonomy as a dial rather than a yes-or-no?

choices.text: Because vendors grade their agent products on a scale from one to five
choices.why: No such scale is used here. The dial is about how many decisions the model holds.

choices.text: Because a model grows more or less sure of its answer from one reply to the next
choices.why: Sureness is about the answer. The dial is about who chooses the steps.

choices.text: Decisions are handed over one at a time
choices.why: Right. Which branch, which tool, which arguments, when to stop: each one is the code's or the model's.

choices.text: Agents learn to need less supervision
choices.why: Nothing in agent.py learns between runs. Each run starts from the same code and an empty conversation.

prompt: Who runs `shop.get_order` when the agent looks up M-1042?

choices.text: The model, on the provider's servers, with the order id it chose itself
choices.why: The model sent back a block naming the tool and its arguments. It has no access to shop.db.

choices.text: Ollama, between reading the request and writing its reply
choices.why: Ollama runs the model and returns text and tool_use blocks. It never touches the shop's database.

choices.text: The Anthropic SDK, automatically, as soon as a tool_use block arrives
choices.why: The SDK sends and receives. agent.py's RUN table is what calls the function.

choices.text: agent.py, on ana's machine
choices.why: Right. The host reads the request and calls the function. The model only asked.

prompt: Through the recorder, Bia's question took two requests: 270 input tokens, then 239. The second carried the first's messages plus a tool call and its result. Why is it smaller?

choices.text: The template wrote the tool descriptions only into the first request
choices.why: Right. llama3.2's template puts the tools inside the last message only when that message is the user's, and the second ended with a tool result.

choices.text: Ollama cached the first request
choices.why: The cached tokens are a column of their own. The input column counts the whole prompt either way.

choices.text: The SDK dropped Bia's message once the model had answered it
choices.why: The recorder shows the request: Bia's message is still the first entry of messages.

choices.text: The system prompt is sent only with the first request of a conversation
choices.why: SYSTEM is passed to every call in agent.py's loop, identical each time.

prompt: Why is an agent's mistake more expensive than an assistant's, given the same model?

choices.text: Agents are billed at a higher rate per token by every provider
choices.why: Providers price by model and token, not by how the program uses them.

choices.text: It acts on the mistake before anyone reads it
choices.why: Right. An assistant's wrong draft is read by somebody; an agent's wrong step becomes the input to the next one.

choices.text: Its model makes more mistakes
choices.why: Same model, same rate of mistakes. What differs is what happens after one.

choices.text: None of its actions can be undone
choices.why: Reading an order can be repeated freely. The point is that nobody checked before it acted.

prompt: Which of these become your problem once a model chooses the steps? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The same question takes a different number of steps on different runs
choices.why: Yes. The number of steps is decided at run time, by the model.

choices.text: The cost of one answer is known only when it is finished
choices.why: Yes. Each step resends the conversation, and the steps are not fixed in advance.

choices.text: A tool is called with arguments nobody wrote
choices.why: Yes. The arguments come from the model's reply.

choices.text: The program needs a network connection to the database
choices.why: No. shop.db is a local file, and the agent changes nothing about how it is reached.

prompt: A colleague tests agent.py by running Bia's question once and checking the answer. Why is one run weak evidence?

choices.text: Because the answer should have been checked by a second model instead of a person
choices.why: Lesson 18 measures over many runs, and one run is weak whoever reads it.

choices.text: Because the help centre will have changed by the time the next run happens
choices.why: The weakness is there even with the help centre frozen, as make_shop.py writes it.

choices.text: One run tests one path, and a real model picks again
choices.why: Right. The path is chosen at run time, so a test covers many runs and many inputs, not one.

choices.text: Real models never repeat an answer
choices.why: Repeating is not the issue; a real model choosing a different path is.

prompt: In this course, where do the model's replies come from?

choices.text: From Anthropic's API, reached with the key in ollama.env
choices.why: The key in ollama.env is a placeholder. The base URL beside it sends every request to Ollama.

choices.text: From all-minilm, the model the help-centre search uses
choices.why: all-minilm turns text into vectors for search_help. It writes no replies.

choices.text: From llama3.2:3b, which Ollama runs on your own computer and serves to the libraries
choices.why: Right. The anthropic and openai libraries are pointed at Ollama, which answers in their formats.

choices.text: From a copy of the model downloaded inside each program
choices.why: The programs hold no model. They send requests to Ollama over HTTP, on 127.0.0.1.

prompt: You switch from Ollama to a provider's paid API. What do you change in this lesson's agent.py?

choices.text: The loop, because a paid model returns tool calls in another shape
choices.why: The anthropic library returns the same blocks from either. The loop reads them the same way.

choices.text: The tools, because a paid model needs shop.py on its own servers
choices.why: No model ever runs a tool. agent.py runs shop.py on your machine whatever answers.

choices.text: The model's name in the program, and the key and base URL in the environment
choices.why: Right. The program names llama3.2:3b; the key and the base URL come from the environment.

choices.text: Nothing: the library picks a model
choices.why: The program names its model. A provider has no model called llama3.2:3b.

prompt: A program stops with `AttributeError: module 'math' has no attribute 'sumprod'` when it searches the help centre. What is wrong?

choices.text: The help centre's vectors were never computed
choices.why: shop.py computes them on the first search. This error comes before any vector is used.

choices.text: The Python that runs it is older than 3.12, the first to have math.sumprod
choices.why: Right. math.sumprod arrived in 3.12, and a virtual environment keeps the Python it was made with.

choices.text: Ollama is not running, so all-minilm cannot answer
choices.why: That fails with a connection error from urllib, not with a missing attribute.

choices.text: numpy is missing
choices.why: shop.py does not use numpy. The multiplication is the standard library's.

prompt: In a new terminal, agent.py stops with `Could not resolve authentication method`. What do you check first?

choices.text: Whether the environment was activated in this terminal
choices.why: Right. ollama.env reaches a shell through .venv/bin/activate, and a new terminal starts without it.

choices.text: Whether llama3.2:3b was pulled into Ollama
choices.why: A missing model is an error from Ollama about the model. Here no request was sent.

choices.text: Whether a firewall blocks traffic on the loopback interface
choices.why: The library stopped before connecting to anything, for want of a key.

choices.text: Whether the API key in ollama.env is still valid
choices.why: Ollama checks no key. The library found none at all, which is a different problem.

prompt: Match each system to who decides its next step.

pairs.left: A cron job that archives old orders
A chat that drafts replies for the support team
pairs.right: A person, after reading the answer

pairs.left: A loop that looks up orders until it can answer

right_distractors: The customer, by choosing the words

prompt: How many requests did agent.py send to the model to answer `Which ways can I pay?`
Put one step of agent.py's loop in order.
items: Send the conversation and the tool definitions to the model
Append the model's reply to the conversation
Run each tool the reply asks for
Append the tool results to the conversation
trap: Running a tool before appending the model's reply leaves a result answering a request the conversation does not contain, and the API refuses that order.
